item.title: The Home Icon
item.description: When I was eight years old, I stumbled upon a drawing board while searching for information about my favorite game. It was more than just an art community; people also shared stories about their pets and everyday lives. I also posted fan art there. Looking back, it was quite rough, but people were very welcoming. The webmaster of the site usually chose the cover art for each month. Being selected was like a small honor, and I used to check the site excitedly every month.

item.title: June-2026
item.description: 2026-06-22 A YouTube channel where a housewife only removes calluses from her own feet and her husband’s feet resumed uploading for the first time in three years. It suddenly became active again just one month after I subscribed. Many viewers commented, “I’ve been waiting for you!” It felt surprisingly niche. 2026-06-14 Even though I don't really like articles written by AI, I used to think that every article had to be written perfectly, so I relied on ChatGPT to write them.

item.title: Finding My Way Back Though Linux
item.description: I was a long-time Windows user, believing it was more practical than a Mac. However, at some point, I began to find the entire ecosystem stifling. There were too many pre-installed apps, intrusive Windows Updates, and the expectation that I would eventually have to replace my computer when support ended, even if it was still perfectly usable. Simply put, it felt outdated and overly centralized. This may have been because I had started managing my own website around the same time.

item.title: May-2026
item.description: 2026-05-29 WordPress is deceptively easy and convenient. Recently, I realized that it is actually more difficult than it looks. Even when implementing a simple script, it is often necessary to take a roundabout approach. It feels unnecessarily complicated; in that sense, it may be too large and complex for a personal website. 2026-05-28 I have observed Japanese website owner communities over the past decade. There are many different types of site owners, and it seems that the proportion of people running static sites and dynamic sites such as WordPress is roughly half and half.
